what: Why the kernel check of cone certificates stops at ~1600 expanded terms, and what does and does not fix it.

measurements.test: isZero (sub (mul q45 q45) (mul q45 q45)) (4050 flat)
collect-as-you-go multiplication (fold, collecting each row), k = 45 and k = 100
measurements.why: The kernel evaluates lazily; the fold's accumulator stays an unevaluated thunk, so collection is deferred to the end and nests exactly as deep.

measurements.test: isZero (sub (mul q45 q45) (mul q45 q45)) with maxRecDepth 20000
measurements.note: Measured under a guard that kills the process above 6 GB or 600 s.
Unguarded; its memory pressure contributed to the machine's C: drive reaching 0.04 GB free, and it was killed. Recorded so nobody repeats it without a guard.

conclusions: The limit is Lean's recursion guard, not a hard wall: raising maxRecDepth lifts it.

A tail-recursive `collect` is NOT the fix. Under lazy kernel evaluation, tail calls with an accumulator build deferred thunks of the same depth. The checker README previously called it 'the obvious fix'; that was wrong and has been corrected.
Raising maxRecDepth inside forge_cone is NOT safe to ship: time and memory grow with the expanded product count (148 s and 4.47 GB at 2025 products).

The fix that scales is algorithmic: Kronecker substitution, checking the identity as a few GMP integer operations at one large point with a proved coefficient bound, so the kernel never expands products. Not implemented: whether it is needed depends on whether real problems exceed the limit, which the tactic head-to-head measures first.
